doc.title: Charles Lloyd — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Producing his own records after The Water Is Wide
summary: Because Higgins was sick, Lloyd and Dorothy insisted on recording in California and have since produced their own ECM records.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: But I’ll tell you something else interesting about that: I didn’t like somebody messing with me so much about that, because that’s what I was doing. And what you are seeing is what I’m doing, and as a result, thanks to Higgins... Higgins was sick during The Water is Wide time period in the early ‘90s, and he wanted to record on his own drums near home, near his temple and stuff like that. Dorothy told Manford we’ll have to make this record in California, and Manford’s not about to come to California. You know, he’s really Nordic. So we started producing our own records from then on.
And he normally doesn’t let people do that.
Cause he’s a great producer and he wants to produce. This stuff has gone to a place where it’s so personal that I don’t think you can mess with it.
